study_identification_part.si4_title: Individual-level deviations from normative brain morphology in violence, psychosis, and psychopathy

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The study clearly states research objectives and hypotheses. (1) Research hypotheses are provided: The authors hypothesize high interindividual anatomical variability in SSD-V with more extreme deviations in regions previously associated with violence (amygdala, hippocampus, orbito-frontal cortex, anterior cingulate cortex), different patterns between SSD-V and SSD-NV, and associations between psychopathy traits and specific deviation patterns. (2) The purpose of applying normative modeling is clearly described: to assess individual brain characteristics in forensic psychiatry populations, to overcome challenges related to small subject samples, and to provide clinicians with individual-level neurobiological information for treatment selection and targeted interventions. Both criteria are satisfied.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "The objective of this study is to assess the potential of normative modeling in forensic psychiatry neuroimaging research by investigating individual patterns of deviations from the norm in persons with a history of severe violence and schizophrenia spectrum disorder (SSD-V), in persons with a schizophrenia spectrum disorder but no history of violence (SSD-NV), persons with a history of severe violence without schizophrenia spectrum disorder (nonSSD-V), and healthy controls with no history of violence (HC). We hypothesize that there will be high interindividual anatomical variability in persons with SSD-V, but with more extreme deviations in regions previously associated with violence in severe mental disorders such as the amygdala, hippocampus, orbito-frontal cortex, and anterior cingulate cortex." ; "using normative modeling in forensic psychiatry neuroimaging studies may overcome inherent challenges related to the small subject samples... and serve as a powerful tool not only to investigate underlying mechanisms of violent behavior in psychosis, but also to provide clinicians with individual level neurobiological information that together with other clinical information/characteristics may inform treatment selection and targeted interventions at the individual level."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "T1-weighted volumes were collected on two GE 3T scanners located at the Oslo University hospital, Norway: (1) GE Signa HDxt scanner with a standard 8-channel head coil, using a sagittal 3D fast spoiled gradient echo (FSPGR) sequence with the following parameters: repetition time (TR) = 7.8 ms, echo time (TE) = 2.9 ms, flip angle 12°, slice thickness 1.2 mm, 166 sagittal slices, field of view (FOV) 256 × 256 mm, acquisition matrix 256 × 192 mm, voxel size = 1 × 1 × 1.2 mm3 and (2) DiscoveryTM MR750 scanner with the vendor's 32-channel head coil, using an inversion recovery-fast spoiled gradient echo sequence (BRAVO) with the following parameters: TR = 8.16 ms, TE = 3.18 ms, TI = 450 ms, flip angle = 12°, FOV = 256 mm, acquisition matrix = 256 × 256 mm, 188 sagittal slices, slice thickness = 1.0 mm, voxel size = 1 × 1× 1 mm3."

nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "Freesurfer v7.1 was used to process data that passed quality control. Subcortical volume segmentation was based on a probabilistic atlas with priors for 31 brain structures." ; "Image quality checking was carried out in two steps. First, all T1w images were processed using MRIqc. Then two trained raters visually examined the scans marked for exclusion by MRIqc pipeline (NT and JR). If the surface values had negative values, unusual patterns, or a significant value imbalance across hemispheres, the individual was removed."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The inclusion criteria for persons with a history of violence (SSD-V and nonSSD-V) were age between 18 and 70 years and a court or hospital record verified episode of severe violence, defined as homicide, attempted homicide, or physical (including sexual) violence towards other persons.
